16	# ADR-0016: A claim's number is the chance it happens by its deadline; whether is solved exactly, when is sampled
17	
18	> **`proposed`.** Both rounds of the stack-05 spike have reported and their numbers are in. One place is still open — the composition place in *How two causes combine* — where an analysis of how causes that are *not* independent should be composed is running, at Kent's request.
19	
20	## Context and Problem Statement
21	
22	Every tile carries a number and the sentence beside it says *the chance this claim comes out true by its deadline*. The engine computes something else — a likelihood read on one day — and three defects follow. All three reproduce on `main` (`d44634a`) under a suite green at 100% coverage of the pure core. They were measured at `48eb562`; `backend/src/katalyst/domain`, where all three live, is byte-identical between the two (`git diff 48eb562 d44634a -- backend/src/katalyst/domain` prints nothing).
23	
24	**What does a number on a tile mean, and what arithmetic works it out?** Re-run 2026-09-21 by this record's author; one command re-runs all three and saves its output beside it (`plans/analysis/scripts/adr-05/`, kept locally).
25	
26	| | What happens | Root cause |
27	|---|---|---|
28	| **1. Telling the map something happened never reaches what caused it** | Two claims, one arrow of strength `1.2`, both at `.30`. **This happened** on the effect leaves the cause at `.3000` where the hand-worked answer is `.4562`, and **Suppose this is true** prints the identical `.3000` — two verbs, one behaviour (`verify_observe.py`). Down a three-claim chain: `.3500` against `.4015`, `.4040` against `.5971` — a miss of `−.1931` (`recheck.py` §3) | The engine keeps each claim's worked-out likelihood and throws away the coin flip (`propagation.py:1470`); for a causeless claim that likelihood is identical in every world, so discarding worlds cannot move it |
29	| **2. The tradeable endings are deaf to half their causes** | On Hormuz, **Suppose the war-risk insurance premium falls** moves *Brent settles below $68* `.3925 → .4759` and moves **both** endings by exactly `0.0000`; supposing OPEC+ restraint moves it to `.2197`, both endings again `0.0000` (`verify_trigger_read_day.py`) | An arrow reads its source on the day the source's **earliest** incoming arrow lands — one integer doing two jobs (`propagation.py:842`, read at `:1463`). For Brent that is day 2; the premium's push lands day 7 and OPEC+'s day 5, *inside* Brent's own series, which is identical through day 6 and separates at day 7, `.492` against `.409` |
30	| **3. A claim nobody believes deletes the reader's own assertion** | Suppose the strait open on 1 October, then insert a claim the map gives one chance in a thousand with a `−0.01` arrow into it: the tile never reads *Supposed* on any day — day-states `withdrawn, withdrawn, pushed, …` from day zero, the number its own prior `.30` throughout (`recheck.py` §1) | A supposition ends on a calendar read off the map's shape (`propagation.py:940-948`), and the test for which arrows oppose it reads only the sign of the push (`:888-895`). Neither the opposing claim's likelihood nor the size of its push enters |
31	
32	**And a range made of coin flips.** With every stated range frozen to a point, so the honest answer is zero width, two claims on a six-claim chain report `.0157` and `.0187`; under **This happened** on a three-claim chain the middle claim reports `.1571` (`recheck.py` §2, §3). *(Record 0014 calls this the band; the vocabulary's word, used here, is the **range**.)*
33	
34	## Decision Drivers
35	
36	* **The traceability veto** (Kent): no state that cannot be traced to an input, a rule or a cited source. A number wrong by `.19` that cannot say so is that state.
37	* **INV-3, assert is not observe** — defect 1 makes the two verbs identical. **INV-4, locality** is kept, and ideally made easier to prove. **INV-7** wants two significant figures, and a second figure that moves with the dice is not one.
38	* **Kent's direction, 2026-09-21**, as the dated decisions note records it: an exact core with a sampler on top, the time model kept and made sound. **Stack 06 needs event days** to say whether a stop is touched before a target.
39	
40	## Considered Options
41	
42	**A.** Repair the defects inside today's engine. · **B.** One variable per claim whose value is *the day it first happened*, solved exactly over those days — one of the two reviews' design. · **C.** A claim's number becomes *the chance it happens by its deadline*; arrows bend a **rate**; *when* comes from one forward pass, *whether* is solved exactly over yes/no truths. · **D.** Do nothing.
43	
44	Three terms, each once. A **rate** (the standard name is a *hazard*) is how likely a claim is to happen on a given day, given it has not happened yet; added up across its window it gives the chance it has happened by the end — a **first passage** probability. **Variable elimination** solves a sparse network of yes/no claims exactly: multiply the small tables and sum out one claim at a time. **Likelihood weighting** is the alternative to discarding inconsistent worlds: keep every world, weighted by how well it matches the evidence.
45	
46	| | Measured | Source |
47	|---|---|---|
48	| **A** | Defect 2 has **no** repair — the right day is per world, so the settled day becomes random, and the grid, the day-states, retraction and the locality proof are built on it being fixed. Defect 1's cheap repair kills the range: a yes/no flag's within-version **variance** is about `0.25` against an across-version `0.01`, so the noise correction clamps to zero and every range under **This happened** collapses to a point. Restoring it needs ~30× the worlds — one `propagate` on the fixture is **66.4 ms** at 2 000 versions × 8 worlds (`8.4 ms` at 250 × 8), so **about 2 s**. 1.5 sessions, `+120 / −60`, defect 3 still standing | engine digest §3a; timings `recheck.py` §5, re-run 2026-09-21 (a run-to-run band: 65.7 and 66.4 ms that day) |
49	| **B** | Generated 20-claim maps, ≤3 causes a claim: **0.7–7.8 s** a range, largest table **4.8–62.7 million entries**; at 30 claims **58–119 s** or out of memory | engine digest §0(2), `ve_cost.py` |
50	| **C** | The engine digest sold this design on **0.5 ms** at 20 claims. **That timed the elimination only:** `ve_cost.py` builds its tables from a random logistic with no time model (`:133-135`), before the clock starts (`:238-239`; clock at `:205`). The pass that builds tables from the arrows was never costed, and it is what the spike killed the design on. Corrected figures below | spike round one, verdict 5; lines re-read on `main` by this record's author |
51	| **D** | Nothing, and a thesis card resting on endings that do not move when half their causes do | defect 2 |
52	
53	**C as first designed, judged against B** — 140 adversarially generated four-claim maps, 9 520 numbers (adversarial pass M1; the spike's faster code reproduces the red team's enumerator to `0.000e+00`):
54	
55	| Query | compared | mean | 99th pct | worst | over `.005` |
56	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
57	| no edit | 560 | `.00027` | `.0046` | `.0175` | 0.9% |
58	| **Suppose this is true** | 4 480 | `.00007` | `.0015` | `.0259` | **0.2%** |
59	| **This happened** | 4 480 | `.00127` | `.0151` | **`.2043`** | **6.6%** |
60	
61	*Suppose this is true* was right from the start; *This happened* was not. The arithmetic is exact, but the **table** is built from timing worked out before the evidence, and evidence moves *when* a cause happened as well as *whether*. It bites when the observed claim is itself a cause of another cause and the reach is through impulse arrows; a plain chain is exact.
62	
63	## Decision Outcome
64	
65	Chosen option: **C with three amendments the spike measured** — an additive rate, a weighted forward sample for *This happened*, and the middle-of-the-slice convention. It is the only option measured to honour both halves of Kent's direction inside the budget he has now named, and the only one that hands stack 06 event days it can trust.
66	
67	**What a number means.** The chance the claim resolves YES by its own deadline — what the tile already says. Not a snapshot on one day, and **an event that has happened never un-happens**.
68	
69	**The time model stays on the arrow.** `strength`, `lag`, `shape`, `half_life` keep their names and meanings and bend a **rate** rather than a likelihood read on one day. An impulse's whole area now counts, so the answer no longer depends on where a deadline falls against a half-life — record 0014's admitted wart; attacked with half-lives of one and two days landing four days before a deadline, the gaps were `.0000` to `.0001`.
70	
71	### How two causes combine — Kent's decision R18
72	
73	**Causes add to a claim's rate: each is an independent route by which the effect may come about.** The chance none of them brings it about is the product of the chances that none severally does — the independent-routes rule a reader can check by hand. A claim at 10% on its own, two causes each of which *alone* would take it to 40% by the same deadline, both happening on day one (`model_diff.py`, round two §4):
74	
75	| | neither | one cause | **both** |
76	|---|---|---|---|
77	| **causes add — independent routes (chosen)** | `.100` | `.392` | **`.590`** |
78	| causes multiply — the first design | `.100` | `.392` | **`.910`** |
79	
80	With no cause the claim fails nine times in ten; one cause cuts that to six in ten, removing a third of the ways it could fail; two independent causes each remove a third, leaving `.40` of the failure. The multiplicative form instead multiplies the rate about fivefold per cause, twenty-five for two.
81	
82	**What is given up: causes never amplify one another.** *Hormuz reopens* and *OPEC+ restraint holds* may really be worth more together than apart, and here they are not. What is not arguable is that **nobody stated the amplification** — the model is asked two numbers per arrow and neither is about two causes coinciding, so the old form put it there itself. Genuine reinforcement needs a third elicited number on the pair, which version one does not have.
83	
84	`<<COMPOSITION: what the analysis recommends for causes that share a route or need each other>>`
85	
86	### How it is worked out
87	
88	1. **The forward pass gives *when*.** Causes first, each claim's chance of having happened by each of 12–24 slices. Because the rate adds, the chance a claim has *not* happened is a product with one factor per cause, so the average is taken **one cause at a time** rather than over every combination of arrival days — the whole of the cost result below. Proved: one cause at a time equals averaging the full table to **`4.4e-16`**, the forward pass agrees to `2.1e-15`, and many versions in one pass equals one at a time to `0.0` (`check.py`, round two §1).
89	2. **Variable elimination gives *whether*, exactly.** **Suppose this is true** pins the claim to its day, redoes the forward pass and solves; **This happened** multiplies in a mask keeping only what agrees with the evidence, and renormalises. The versions ride as an array axis, so a range is one pass.
90	3. **A weighted forward sample answers *This happened*.** Worlds are drawn forward with arrival days; at the observed claim the world is not thrown away — the claim is set to what was observed and the world's weight multiplied by how likely that was. **The exact yes/no solve is the control variate**: the same world is drawn twice, once under the full time model and once under the yes/no model with the same random numbers, so only the *difference* is sampled and added to an answer already known exactly. Seeded. **One sample serves a whole range, and both readers** — the numbers on screen and the event days stack 06 reads.
91	4. **An arrival inside a slice is taken at the slice's middle, not its end.** One line; at 24 slices it moves the worst gap against a fine reference from `.0290` to **`.0027`**, and the last-day convention at 60 slices is worse than the middle-day one at 12 (`midpoint.py`, `convergence.py`).
92	
93	Two properties become facts rather than machinery: **locality becomes a theorem**, a claim cut off from the evidence having a factor that sums to one; and **the width shares** (FR-21) become exact, one extra solve each. **Observations stay undated in version one** — `Observe` carries a target and a value and no date (`intervention.py:70-85`), and *this happened on day 5* would need the yes/no question re-cut per evidence day.
94	
95	### The kill criterion, and Kent's new budget
96	
97	> *A candidate passes if it holds `.005` on 99% of the adversarial set **and** runs inside 300 ms on a 20-claim map (up to 3 causes a claim) for one world with its range.*
98	
99	**It fired, twice. This record does not claim the 300 ms criterion was met.**
100	
101	| | accuracy, *This happened*, 4 480 numbers | one world with its range, 20 claims |
102	|---|---|---|
103	| **round one** — multiplicative rate | sample + control variate: 99.98% at 50 000 worlds, 100.00% at 200 000 | **3.0 s at 200 versions**, 12 slices. The binding cost was the shared forward pass at **2 879 ms**, not the sampler at 110 ms; at 24 slices that pass is 208 ms for *one* version |
104	| **round two** — additive rate: the tables alone | mean `.00103`, 99th pct `.0127`, worst `.0420`, **5.36% over `.005`** — better than `.2043`, still failing | 39 ms at 200 versions · 305 ms at 2 000 |
105	| **round two** — additive rate: the sample + control variate, 50 000 worlds | mean `.00028`, 99th pct `.0020`, worst **`.0042`**, **0.00% over `.005`**; *no edit* worst `.0025`, *Suppose* worst `.0027` | **97 ms at 200 versions · 360 ms at 2 000**; with three claims held back by an arrow, 113 ms and **538 ms** |
106	
107	*(`candidates_add.py`, `timing20.py`, `timing_add.py`; round two at 24 slices throughout.)* The additive rate improves the tables markedly and still fails the 99% bar, **so the sampler is required**. Its effective sample size is 96.9% of the worlds drawn on average, 42.9% at worst. **The other candidates, one line each:** keeping the prior-timing tables is the second row, which fails; re-cutting the yes/no variable per evidence day leaves 4.38% over `.005` and can be *worse* than doing nothing, and the widening that does pass widens three claims of four — option **B** with one sink left over, at B's cost (round one §2).
108	
109	Round one's miss was 10×; round two's is 1.2×. **Kent relaxed the budget to 600 ms for one world with its range at 2 000 versions** (decision R19), with these measurements in front of him. Every configuration is inside it even at the slow end of the sampler's own run-to-run band — the 50 000-world timings in `timing_add.log` span **52 to 95 ms**, and the totals above use the fast end, so the slow end gives about 399 ms and 578 ms.
110	
111	**Why the sample is a fixed cost, not a per-version one.** Its correction is shared across a range. Round one measured that on easy maps only and flagged the hard one; round two measured the hard one (trial 33, `hardmap.py`): under the multiplicative rate the correction is `.1172` and moves `.0805` between versions, so sharing would have been wrong by up to `.08` on a band end. **Under the additive rate it is `.0020` and moves `.0020`.** Redone per version, 2 000 versions would cost 110 seconds.
112	
113	**And a range needs 2 000 versions.** Round one solved 20 000 versions of the same map exactly under an observation and resampled from that pool (`versions.py` §6): at **2 000** a band end wanders `.0086` on a wide band and `.0046` on a narrow one — 3% of the band's own width; at **200**, the count the engine digest proposed, it wanders `.0275`, a tenth of the width, which is one significant figure. **Keep 2 000; the inner eight worlds go, the outer loop does not.** *(Measured under the multiplicative rate and not re-run under the additive one, so it could move — round two §7.)*
114	
115	### What `World.series` now means, and what stays
116	
117	Today `series` is a per-day likelihood allowed to **fall**, and the golden test pins it (`test_hormuz_golden.py:117-120`): `1.0 → .36 → .36 → <.10`. **Under "the chance it has happened by day *t*" a series can only rise**, so that test cannot survive; the events-and-states reading of the same branch replaces it, proposed record 0017's to write. An event's series is a rising curve; the field keeps its name and type, and days between grid points are read off the same added-up rate rather than re-solved (`propagation.py:110`, `SERIES_CAP = 180`). Two smaller consequences are carried in full by the owed-edits list: `DeltaRow.peak_delta` and `at_day` keep their arithmetic and lose their stated rationale, written for a curve that unwinds (`diff.py:239-252`); and the golden domino assertion (`:81`) passes by construction under a rising curve and is restated as a comparison between branches on one day.
118	
119	**A supposed claim's stored `p = 1.0` stays** — three live readers, not the one the first draft assumed: `diff.py:817-818`, `diff.py:460`, `frontend/src/world/apiSource.ts:266`. `Belief.p` allows no gap (`belief.py:39-45`), so removing it is a wire break.
120	
121	**What this record amends:** **ADR-0005** and **ADR-0014**, neither superseded — 0005's aggregation formula and execution paragraph (arrows now bend an **additive rate**), its learning rule and its definition of a belief; 0014's section B machinery, its section F entirely, its section E wart and its 2026-09-17 weighting rule. **What `lo` and `hi` mean does not change**, which is what 0014 is for; **ADR-0015 is untouched**. *The dated amendments appended to both in this pull request say it sentence by sentence.*
122	
123	### Consequences
124	
125	* Good, because the number answers the sentence beside it, **This happened** does something, and supposing any cause on Hormuz moves what it points at.
126	* Good, because locality becomes a property of the arithmetic and its oracle can get **stricter**, and with every stated range frozen to a point the range is zero by construction.
127	* Good, because stack 06 gets event days it can trust: measured against the judge over 40 maps (`when_table.py`, round one §7), the weighted sample's day distributions are within `.0064` of exact at worst and its median arrival is at most **one slice** out, where drawing truths exactly and then days under the prior moves a median arrival by **four slices — ten days**, worst distribution gap `.2143`. *(Measured under the multiplicative rate; the sampler's construction is unchanged but this was not re-run.)*
128	* Bad, because **every number on the map changes once** — hence a flip of its own, reviewed as one file's diff.
129	* Bad, because causes no longer amplify one another, and no version-one map can say that two of them do.
130	* Bad, because the 300 ms criterion was not met: the budget was relaxed to fit the measurements rather than the measurements fitting the budget.
131	* Neutral, because the wire shapes keep their names and types — `series` and `moved_only_by_reweighting` change what they carry, and `Verdict.product` becomes always empty under record 0022.
132	
133	### Still open, and where it can go wrong
134	
135	* **An arrow that holds a claim back is the one place the cost still multiplies**, forcing an enumeration over the days it might have arrived on. On the same map: three such arrows cost **1.8×** the forward pass, eight `5.4×`, the generator's own ten **70×** — 15.9 s at 2 000 versions (`inhibitors.py`, `timing_add.py`). Real maps carry at most one per claim today, which is why 538 ms is the honest worst case — **but the freeze intends to add a *what would stop this step* sentence to the prompt, which will raise that count**, and nobody has measured the map it produces. The lever is a cap per claim; it is not proposed here because there is nothing yet to size it against. **They also saturate:** an arrow cannot hold a claim back on days it is not on, so **30.0%** of the holding-back arrows in the adversarial set were clamped short of their stated chance (`candidates_add.py`).
136	* **Accuracy is measured on four-claim maps only** — the judge is not computable above that — while the cost numbers are from twenty-claim maps; the two sets never meet.
137	* **Unmeasured headroom, named so nobody guesses:** the exact solve runs one elimination per claim, twenty passes, 80 ms at 2 000 versions; two passes over a junction tree would land the whole thing near 295 ms. Not built, not measured. And proposed record 0017's states sweep is being re-run under the additive rate; that record carries the place for it.
138	
139	### Confirmation
140	
141	**Two oracles, two tolerances, proving two different things.** One alone could not have caught the error above: an enumerator built from the core's own tables proves the summing and is blind to a wrong table.
142	
143	1. **`test_the_elimination_is_exact`** — tolerance `1e-9`, over the core's **own** yes/no tables, summing the joint by hand. Proves the elimination, the supposition surgery and the conditioning. Blind to timing.
144	2. **`test_the_tables_agree_with_integrating_over_time`** — forbidden the core's tables, built from the arrow parameters alone, enumerating the full joint of event times on maps of four claims or fewer. Tolerance **`.005` on each of the three questions, with the sample size named**: at **50 000 worlds** the measured worsts are `.0025` no edit, `.0027` *Suppose*, `.0042` *This happened* (round two §2); at 200 000 they are `.0013`, `.0014`, `.0020` (round one §8). **Two conditions:** the enumerator runs at the **same number of slices and the same within-slice convention** as the core — 24 slices judged by 60 with a different convention differs by `.0290` on its own, swallowing the tolerance — and **the sample is seeded**, so the test is deterministic.
145	
146	**The locality oracle, restated and stricter:** *cut off from the evidence ⇒ bit for bit* — byte-identical, not merely close. `test_band_is_not_sampling_noise` survives and tightens to zero width exactly. `test_an_observation_moves_a_cause_even_when_no_arrow_pushes` (`test_propagation.py:544`) is **reversed into an assertion of invariance**: record 0014's 2026-09-17 amendment decided deliberately that an observation moves a causeless claim through the version weights; this record removes the mechanism.
147	
148	### How it lands
149	
150	| Step | Contents | `main` after |
151	|---|---|---|
152	| **1** | The two oracles and their enumerators, the second committed under `backend/tests/`. Failing cases marked strictly expected-to-fail, by name. Reverse the invariance test. | Green. Two tests documenting two defects. |
153	| **2** | The new core beside the old, behind a flag, **default unchanged**. Both oracles run against both. | Green. **Every screen still shows today's numbers.** |
154	| **3** | **The flip, alone.** Default changes; Hormuz re-derived; the generated numbers file regenerated — **its diff is the complete, reviewable statement of which numbers moved**. The two nested loops, the noise correction, the version weights and `moved_only_by_reweighting` go; `diff.py` moves over; the browser's three rendering readers of that flag (`graph/diff/noChange.ts:52`, `Inspector.tsx:248` and `:385`), its mapper (`apiSource.ts:325`) and its *"worlds under each"* sentence (`apiSource.ts:228`) are corrected. | Green. Every number changes **once**. |
155	| **4** | Separately: record 0022's three quantities, and record 0017's events and states. | Green. |
156	
157	The generated numbers file must exist *before* step 3, or the flip also carries a sweep of several hundred numbers across the chapters and nobody can review it.
158	
159	### Honest cost
160	
161	**Five to seven sessions for this record's work** (adversarial pass M5; a session is about three focused hours); record 0017's events and states add about **1.3** (engine digest §5.3), so **six to nine together**; the whole of stack 05 about **nine and a half** (S4) — which also notes this repository has never kept session accounts, so every figure is a first estimate.
162	
163	What the first estimate of three missed, verified on `main`: **`diff.py`**, 1 459 lines, where the version weights, the reweighting flag, the range import, the sweep's reading of retractions and the ranked list's reading of `series` die or change; **the browser**, budgeted at zero — the readers in step 3, plus the retraction badge whose height is baked into the tile's geometry; **34 of `test_propagation.py`'s 46** tests (46 confirmed by count); **the locality oracle**, rewritten and stricter; and **every decimal in the two multiverse chapters** — 259 in `propagation.md`, 189 in `diff.md`, counted as a decimal point with two or more digits after it. For calibration, `d9c853e` (#38) fixed **one** defect class and cost **1 335 insertions across 12 files**.
164	
165	## Open for Kent
166	
167	**What the screen says about *This happened*.** The sampler is seeded and reproducible and no measured number is off by more than `.005`, but it is a sample, and the reader is entitled to know which verb is answered by one.
168	
169	* *Recommended:* nothing on the ordinary screen, and one sentence in the Inspector on an observation branch — *"learning moves numbers upstream; this one is worked out by a seeded sample of 50 000 worlds and is within `.005` of the exact answer on maps this size."*
170	* Alternative: say it on the honesty line for every world — cheaper, and it puts a caveat on screens the caveat is not about. Or say nothing anywhere, which is the traceability veto.
171	
172	## Pros and Cons of the Options
173	
174	The cost table above carries each option's case; one line each.
175	
176	* **A.** Smallest change, one file — and it buys back neither defect 1's range nor defect 2 at all, leaving defect 3, the path product and claims that un-resolve.
177	* **B.** **The model is right and this design adopts it**: its calibration reproduces the two elicited numbers to four places and observing a claim gives exact Bayes upstream. Only the *inference* is rejected — seconds to minutes a range against any budget named here, which a seven-claim prototype cannot see.
178	* **C with the spike's three amendments, chosen.** Exact for *Suppose this is true*, within `.005` everywhere measured for *This happened*, inside the budget, and event days right to one slice. Against: causes cannot amplify one another; an arrow that holds a claim back is still expensive and 30% saturate; accuracy is measured on four claims only.
179	* **D.** The card would rest on endings deaf to half their causes, and a second verb that prints the first verb's answer.
180	
181	## More Information
182	
183	* **Kent's decisions, 2026-09-21**, recorded in the dated decisions note kept locally under `plans/notes/`: **R1** (an exact core with a sampler on top, the time model kept and made sound, a spike with a kill criterion first), **R18** (causes add as independent routes, with an analysis of non-independent causes commissioned) and **R19** (the budget is 600 ms for one world with its range at 2 000 versions). *(Those are the decisions note's words for his choices, not a transcript of his own.)*
184	* **The evidence.** The stack-05 spike, both rounds, and the engine digest and adversarial pass that preceded them, all 2026-09-21, kept locally under `plans/analysis/` with their scripts. Every measurement here is quoted from one of those reports with its script named, or was re-run on 2026-09-21 by this record's author.
185	* **Related.** ADR-0005 and ADR-0014 (amended, not superseded) · ADR-0015 (intact) · proposed ADR-0017, ADR-0021, ADR-0022. Chapters rewritten: `spec/multiverse/propagation.md`, `spec/multiverse/diff.md`.
186

# ADR-0016: A claim's number is the chance it happens by its deadline; whether is solved exactly, when is sampled

> **`proposed`.** Both rounds of the stack-05 spike have reported and their numbers are in. One place is still open — the composition place in *How two causes combine* — where an analysis of how causes that are *not* independent should be composed is running, at Kent's request.

## Context and Problem Statement

Every tile carries a number and the sentence beside it says *the chance this claim comes out true by its deadline*. * **The traceability veto** (Kent): no state that cannot be traced to an input, a rule or a cited source. A number wrong by `.19` that cannot say so is that state.

* **Kent's direction, 2026-09-21**, as the dated decisions note records it: an exact core with a sampler on top, the time model kept and made sound. **Stack 06 needs event days** to say whether a stop is touched before a target.

## Considered Options

**A.** Repair the defects inside today's engine. · **B.** One variable per claim whose value is *the day it first happened*, solved exactly over those days — one of the two reviews' design. · **C.** A claim's number becomes *the chance it happens by its deadline*; arrows bend a **rate**; *when* comes from one forward pass, *whether* is solved exactly over yes/no truths. · **D.** Do nothing.

Three terms, each once. A **rate** (the standard name is a *hazard*) is how likely a claim is to happen on a given day, given it has not happened yet; added up across its window it gives the chance it has happened by the end — a **first passage** probability. **Variable elimination** solves a sparse network of yes/no claims exactly: multiply the small tables and sum out one claim at a time. **Likelihood weighting** is the alternative to discarding inconsistent worlds: keep every world, weighted by how well it matches the evidence.

## Decision Outcome

Chosen option: **C with three amendments the spike measured** — an additive rate, a weighted forward sample for *This happened*, and the middle-of-the-slice convention. It is the only option measured to honour both halves of Kent's direction inside the budget he has now named, and the only one that hands stack 06 event days it can trust.

**What a number means.** The chance the claim resolves YES by its own deadline — what the tile already says. Not a snapshot on one day, and **an event that has happened never un-happens**.

**The time model stays on the arrow.** `strength`, `lag`, `shape`, `half_life` keep their names and meanings and bend a **rate** rather than a likelihood read on one day. An impulse's whole area now counts, so the answer no longer depends on where a deadline falls against a half-life — record 0014's admitted wart; attacked with half-lives of one and two days landing four days before a deadline, the gaps were `.0000` to `.0001`.

### How two causes combine — Kent's decision R18

**Causes add to a claim's rate: each is an independent route by which the effect may come about.** The chance none of them brings it about is the product of the chances that none severally does — the independent-routes rule a reader can check by hand. A claim at 10% on its own, two causes each of which *alone* would take it to 40% by the same deadline, both happening on day one (`model_diff.py`, round two §4):

| | neither | one cause | **both** |
|---|---|---|---|
| **causes add — independent routes (chosen)** | `.100` | `.392` | **`.590`** |
| causes multiply — the first design | `.100` | `.392` | **`.910`** |

With no cause the claim fails nine times in ten; one cause cuts that to six in ten, removing a third of the ways it could fail; two independent causes each remove a third, leaving `.40` of the failure. The multiplicative form instead multiplies the rate about fivefold per cause, twenty-five for two.

**What is given up: causes never amplify one another.** *Hormuz reopens* and *OPEC+ restraint holds* may really be worth more together than apart, and here they are not. What is not arguable is that **nobody stated the amplification** — the model is asked two numbers per arrow and neither is about two causes coinciding, so the old form put it there itself. Genuine reinforcement needs a third elicited number on the pair, which version one does not have.

`<<COMPOSITION: what the analysis recommends for causes that share a route or need each other>>`

### How it is worked out

1. **The forward pass gives *when*.** Causes first, each claim's chance of having happened by each of 12–24 slices. Because the rate adds, the chance a claim has *not* happened is a product with one factor per cause, so the average is taken **one cause at a time** rather than over every combination of arrival days — the whole of the cost result below. Proved: one cause at a time equals averaging the full table to **`4.4e-16`**, the forward pass agrees to `2.1e-15`, and many versions in one pass equals one at a time to `0.0` (`check.py`, round two §1).
2. **Variable elimination gives *whether*, exactly.** **Suppose this is true** pins the claim to its day, redoes the forward pass and solves; **This happened** multiplies in a mask keeping only what agrees with the evidence, and renormalises. The versions ride as an array axis, so a range is one pass.
3. **A weighted forward sample answers *This happened*.** Worlds are drawn forward with arrival days; at the observed claim the world is not thrown away — the claim is set to what was observed and the world's weight multiplied by how likely that was. **The exact yes/no solve is the control variate**: the same world is drawn twice, once under the full time model and once under the yes/no model with the same random numbers, so only the *difference* is sampled and added to an answer already known exactly. Seeded. **One sample serves a whole range, and both readers** — the numbers on screen and the event days stack 06 reads.
4. **An arrival inside a slice is taken at the slice's middle, not its end.** One line; at 24 slices it moves the worst gap against a fine reference from `.0290` to **`.0027`**, and the last-day convention at 60 slices is worse than the middle-day one at 12 (`midpoint.py`, `convergence.py`).

Two properties become facts rather than machinery: **locality becomes a theorem**, a claim cut off from the evidence having a factor that sums to one; and **the width shares** (FR-21) become exact, one extra solve each. **Observations stay undated in version one** — `Observe` carries a target and a value and no date (`intervention.py:70-85`), and *this happened on day 5* would need the yes/no question re-cut per evidence day.

### The kill criterion, and Kent's new budget

> *A candidate passes if it holds `.005` on 99% of the adversarial set **and** runs inside 300 ms on a 20-claim map (up to 3 causes a claim) for one world with its range.*

**It fired, twice. This record does not claim the 300 ms criterion was met.**

| | accuracy, *This happened*, 4 480 numbers | one world with its range, 20 claims |
|---|---|---|
| **round one** — multiplicative rate | sample + control variate: 99.98% at 50 000 worlds, 100.00% at 200 000 | **3.0 s at 200 versions**, 12 slices. The binding cost was the shared forward pass at **2 879 ms**, not the sampler at 110 ms; at 24 slices that pass is 208 ms for *one* version |
| **round two** — additive rate: the tables alone | mean `.00103`, 99th pct `.0127`, worst `.0420`, **5.36% over `.005`** — better than `.2043`, still failing | 39 ms at 200 versions · 305 ms at 2 000 |
| **round two** — additive rate: the sample + control variate, 50 000 worlds | mean `.00028`, 99th pct `.0020`, worst **`.0042`**, **0.00% over `.005`**; *no edit* worst `.0025`, *Suppose* worst `.0027` | **97 ms at 200 versions · 360 ms at 2 000**; with three claims held back by an arrow, 113 ms and **538 ms** |

*(`candidates_add.py`, `timing20.py`, `timing_add.py`; round two at 24 slices throughout.)* The additive rate improves the tables markedly and still fails the 99% bar, **so the sampler is required**. Its effective sample size is 96.9% of the worlds drawn on average, 42.9% at worst. **The other candidates, one line each:** keeping the prior-timing tables is the second row, which fails; re-cutting the yes/no variable per evidence day leaves 4.38% over `.005` and can be *worse* than doing nothing, and the widening that does pass widens three claims of four — option **B** with one sink left over, at B's cost (round one §2).

Round one's miss was 10×; round two's is 1.2×. **Kent relaxed the budget to 600 ms for one world with its range at 2 000 versions** (decision R19), with these measurements in front of him. Every configuration is inside it even at the slow end of the sampler's own run-to-run band — the 50 000-world timings in `timing_add.log` span **52 to 95 ms**, and the totals above use the fast end, so the slow end gives about 399 ms and 578 ms.

**Why the sample is a fixed cost, not a per-version one.** Its correction is shared across a range. Round one measured that on easy maps only and flagged the hard one; round two measured the hard one (trial 33, `hardmap.py`): under the multiplicative rate the correction is `.1172` and moves `.0805` between versions, so sharing would have been wrong by up to `.08` on a band end. **Under the additive rate it is `.0020` and moves `.0020`.** Redone per version, 2 000 versions would cost 110 seconds.

**And a range needs 2 000 versions.** Round one solved 20 000 versions of the same map exactly under an observation and resampled from that pool (`versions.py` §6): at **2 000** a band end wanders `.0086` on a wide band and `.0046` on a narrow one — 3% of the band's own width; at **200**, the count the engine digest proposed, it wanders `.0275`, a tenth of the width, which is one significant figure. **Keep 2 000; the inner eight worlds go, the outer loop does not.** *(Measured under the multiplicative rate and not re-run under the additive one, so it could move — round two §7.)*

### What `World.series` now means, and what stays

Today `series` is a per-day likelihood allowed to **fall**, and the golden test pins it (`test_hormuz_golden.py:117-120`): `1.0 → .36 → .36 → <.10`. **Under "the chance it has happened by day *t*" a series can only rise**, so that test cannot survive; the events-and-states reading of the same branch replaces it, proposed record 0017's to write. An event's series is a rising curve; the field keeps its name and type, and days between grid points are read off the same added-up rate rather than re-solved (`propagation.py:110`, `SERIES_CAP = 180`). Two smaller consequences are carried in full by the owed-edits list: `DeltaRow.peak_delta` and `at_day` keep their arithmetic and lose their stated rationale, written for a curve that unwinds (`diff.py:239-252`); and the golden domino assertion (`:81`) passes by construction under a rising curve and is restated as a comparison between branches on one day.

**A supposed claim's stored `p = 1.0` stays** — three live readers, not the one the first draft assumed: `diff.py:817-818`, `diff.py:460`, `frontend/src/world/apiSource.ts:266`. `Belief.p` allows no gap (`belief.py:39-45`), so removing it is a wire break.

**What this record amends:** **ADR-0005** and **ADR-0014**, neither superseded — 0005's aggregation formula and execution paragraph (arrows now bend an **additive rate**), its learning rule and its definition of a belief; 0014's section B machinery, its section F entirely, its section E wart and its 2026-09-17 weighting rule. **What `lo` and `hi` mean does not change**, which is what 0014 is for; **ADR-0015 is untouched**. *The dated amendments appended to both in this pull request say it sentence by sentence.*

### Consequences

* Good, because the number answers the sentence beside it, **This happened** does something, and supposing any cause on Hormuz moves what it points at.
* Good, because locality becomes a property of the arithmetic and its oracle can get **stricter**, and with every stated range frozen to a point the range is zero by construction.
* Good, because stack 06 gets event days it can trust: measured against the judge over 40 maps (`when_table.py`, round one §7), the weighted sample's day distributions are within `.0064` of exact at worst and its median arrival is at most **one slice** out, where drawing truths exactly and then days under the prior moves a median arrival by **four slices — ten days**, worst distribution gap `.2143`. *(Measured under the multiplicative rate; the sampler's construction is unchanged but this was not re-run.)*
* Bad, because **every number on the map changes once** — hence a flip of its own, reviewed as one file's diff.
* Bad, because causes no longer amplify one another, and no version-one map can say that two of them do.
* Bad, because the 300 ms criterion was not met: the budget was relaxed to fit the measurements rather than the measurements fitting the budget.
* Neutral, because the wire shapes keep their names and types — `series` and `moved_only_by_reweighting` change what they carry, and `Verdict.product` becomes always empty under record 0022.

### Still open, and where it can go wrong

* **An arrow that holds a claim back is the one place the cost still multiplies**, forcing an enumeration over the days it might have arrived on. On the same map: three such arrows cost **1.8×** the forward pass, eight `5.4×`, the generator's own ten **70×** — 15.9 s at 2 000 versions (`inhibitors.py`, `timing_add.py`). Real maps carry at most one per claim today, which is why 538 ms is the honest worst case — **but the freeze intends to add a *what would stop this step* sentence to the prompt, which will raise that count**, and nobody has measured the map it produces. The lever is a cap per claim; it is not proposed here because there is nothing yet to size it against. **They also saturate:** an arrow cannot hold a claim back on days it is not on, so **30.0%** of the holding-back arrows in the adversarial set were clamped short of their stated chance (`candidates_add.py`).
* **Accuracy is measured on four-claim maps only** — the judge is not computable above that — while the cost numbers are from twenty-claim maps; the two sets never meet.
* **Unmeasured headroom, named so nobody guesses:** the exact solve runs one elimination per claim, twenty passes, 80 ms at 2 000 versions; two passes over a junction tree would land the whole thing near 295 ms. Not built, not measured. And proposed record 0017's states sweep is being re-run under the additive rate; that record carries the place for it.

### Confirmation

**Two oracles, two tolerances, proving two different things.** One alone could not have caught the error above: an enumerator built from the core's own tables proves the summing and is blind to a wrong table.

1. **`test_the_elimination_is_exact`** — tolerance `1e-9`, over the core's **own** yes/no tables, summing the joint by hand. Proves the elimination, the supposition surgery and the conditioning. Blind to timing.
2. **`test_the_tables_agree_with_integrating_over_time`** — forbidden the core's tables, built from the arrow parameters alone, enumerating the full joint of event times on maps of four claims or fewer. Tolerance **`.005` on each of the three questions, with the sample size named**: at **50 000 worlds** the measured worsts are `.0025` no edit, `.0027` *Suppose*, `.0042` *This happened* (round two §2); at 200 000 they are `.0013`, `.0014`, `.0020` (round one §8). **Two conditions:** the enumerator runs at the **same number of slices and the same within-slice convention** as the core — 24 slices judged by 60 with a different convention differs by `.0290` on its own, swallowing the tolerance — and **the sample is seeded**, so the test is deterministic.

**The locality oracle, restated and stricter:** *cut off from the evidence ⇒ bit for bit* — byte-identical, not merely close. `test_band_is_not_sampling_noise` survives and tightens to zero width exactly. `test_an_observation_moves_a_cause_even_when_no_arrow_pushes` (`test_propagation.py:544`) is **reversed into an assertion of invariance**: record 0014's 2026-09-17 amendment decided deliberately that an observation moves a causeless claim through the version weights; this record removes the mechanism.

### How it lands

| Step | Contents | `main` after |
|---|---|---|
| **1** | The two oracles and their enumerators, the second committed under `backend/tests/`. Failing cases marked strictly expected-to-fail, by name. Reverse the invariance test. | Green. Two tests documenting two defects. |
| **2** | The new core beside the old, behind a flag, **default unchanged**. Both oracles run against both. | Green. **Every screen still shows today's numbers.** |
| **3** | **The flip, alone.** Default changes; Hormuz re-derived; the generated numbers file regenerated — **its diff is the complete, reviewable statement of which numbers moved**. The two nested loops, the noise correction, the version weights and `moved_only_by_reweighting` go; `diff.py` moves over; the browser's three rendering readers of that flag (`graph/diff/noChange.ts:52`, `Inspector.tsx:248` and `:385`), its mapper (`apiSource.ts:325`) and its *"worlds under each"* sentence (`apiSource.ts:228`) are corrected. | Green. Every number changes **once**. |
| **4** | Separately: record 0022's three quantities, and record 0017's events and states. | Green. |

The generated numbers file must exist *before* step 3, or the flip also carries a sweep of several hundred numbers across the chapters and nobody can review it.

### Honest cost

**Five to seven sessions for this record's work** (adversarial pass M5; a session is about three focused hours); record 0017's events and states add about **1.3** (engine digest §5.3), so **six to nine together**; the whole of stack 05 about **nine and a half** (S4) — which also notes this repository has never kept session accounts, so every figure is a first estimate.

What the first estimate of three missed, verified on `main`: **`diff.py`**, 1 459 lines, where the version weights, the reweighting flag, the range import, the sweep's reading of retractions and the ranked list's reading of `series` die or change; **the browser**, budgeted at zero — the readers in step 3, plus the retraction badge whose height is baked into the tile's geometry; **34 of `test_propagation.py`'s 46** tests (46 confirmed by count); **the locality oracle**, rewritten and stricter; and **every decimal in the two multiverse chapters** — 259 in `propagation.md`, 189 in `diff.md`, counted as a decimal point with two or more digits after it. For calibration, `d9c853e` (#38) fixed **one** defect class and cost **1 335 insertions across 12 files**.

## Open for Kent

**What the screen says about *This happened*.** The sampler is seeded and reproducible and no measured number is off by more than `.005`, but it is a sample, and the reader is entitled to know which verb is answered by one.

* *Recommended:* nothing on the ordinary screen, and one sentence in the Inspector on an observation branch — *"learning moves numbers upstream; this one is worked out by a seeded sample of 50 000 worlds and is within `.005` of the exact answer on maps this size."*
* Alternative: say it on the honesty line for every world — cheaper, and it puts a caveat on screens the caveat is not about. Or say nothing anywhere, which is the traceability veto.

## Pros and Cons of the Options

The cost table above carries each option's case; one line each.

* **A.** Smallest change, one file — and it buys back neither defect 1's range nor defect 2 at all, leaving defect 3, the path product and claims that un-resolve.
* **B.** **The model is right and this design adopts it**: its calibration reproduces the two elicited numbers to four places and observing a claim gives exact Bayes upstream. Only the *inference* is rejected — seconds to minutes a range against any budget named here, which a seven-claim prototype cannot see.
* **C with the spike's three amendments, chosen.** Exact for *Suppose this is true*, within `.005` everywhere measured for *This happened*, inside the budget, and event days right to one slice. Against: causes cannot amplify one another; an arrow that holds a claim back is still expensive and 30% saturate; accuracy is measured on four claims only.
* **D.** The card would rest on endings deaf to half their causes, and a second verb that prints the first verb's answer.

## More Information

* **Kent's decisions, 2026-09-21**, recorded in the dated decisions note kept locally under `plans/notes/`: **R1** (an exact core with a sampler on top, the time model kept and made sound, a spike with a kill criterion first), **R18** (causes add as independent routes, with an analysis of non-independent causes commissioned) and **R19** (the budget is 600 ms for one world with its range at 2 000 versions). *(Those are the decisions note's words for his choices, not a transcript of his own.)*
* **The evidence.** The stack-05 spike, both rounds, and the engine digest and adversarial pass that preceded them, all 2026-09-21, kept locally under `plans/analysis/` with their scripts. Every measurement here is quoted from one of those reports with its script named, or was re-run on 2026-09-21 by this record's author.
* **Related.** ADR-0005 and ADR-0014 (amended, not superseded) · ADR-0015 (intact) · proposed ADR-0017, ADR-0021, ADR-0022. Chapters rewritten: `spec/multiverse/propagation.md`, `spec/multiverse/diff.md`.

51	|---|---|
52	| **one cause at a time == averaging the full table over combinations of causes** | **4.4e-16** |
53	| **the forward pass agrees with the same full-table average** | **2.1e-15** |
54	| **many versions in one pass == one version at a time** | **0.0** |
55	
56	Those three are the hypothesis's actual claims, and they hold to machine precision.
57	
58	Two more compare the slice machinery with a dense integral of the rate itself. What is left there
59	is the **slice grid**, which the additive and multiplicative models share, and it shrinks as the
60	slices multiply:
61	
62	| slices × points inside each | calibration reproduces its stated chances to | the machinery is the rate to |
63	|---|---|---|
64	| 24 × 8 | 1.8e-2 | 1.9e-2 |
65	| 24 × 32 | 5.5e-3 | 4.6e-3 |
66	| 48 × 8 | 6.4e-3 | 8.3e-3 |
67	| 48 × 32 | 1.8e-3 | 2.7e-3 |
68	
69	The hard case is a spiky impulse — a half-life of about a day against a slice 2.5 days wide. Round
70	one measured the same effect on the multiplicative model and it is the reason its §4 recommends the
71	middle-day convention, which is used throughout here.
72	
73	---
74	
75	## 2. The kill criterion again, literally
76	
77	### The accuracy half — `candidates_add.py`
78	
79	The same 140 adversarial four-claim maps as round one, the same stated chances, 24 slices, the
80	middle-day convention, 17 queries each — read under the additive rate, judged by the same
81	method (exact over the whole joint of arrival slices, given the additive tables).
82	
83	| *This happened*, 4 480 numbers | mean | 99th pct | worst | share > .005 |
84	|---|---|---|---|---|
85	| **(b) the design's prior-timing tables** | .00103 | .0127 | **.0420** | **5.36%** |
86	| (a) sample 50 000, read straight off the worlds | .00120 | .0053 | .0103 | 1.43% |
87	| **(a) sample 50 000, with the control variate** | .00028 | .0020 | **.0042** | **0.00%** |
88	| (a) sample 200 000, with the control variate | .00014 | .0010 | .0017 | 0.00% |
89	
90	| no edit (560) | mean | 99th pct | worst | > .005 |
91	|---|---|---|---|---|
92	| (b) the design's tables | .00019 | .0039 | .0117 | 0.71% |
93	| (a) sample 50 000, corrected | .00033 | .0019 | .0025 | 0.00% |
94	
95	| *Suppose this is true* (4 480) | mean | 99th pct | worst | > .005 |
96	|---|---|---|---|---|
97	| (b) the design's tables | .00004 | .0010 | .0116 | 0.13% |
98	| (a) sample 50 000, corrected | .00017 | .0015 | .0027 | 0.00% |
99	
100	Effective sample size — how many equally-weighted worlds the weighted sample is worth — is **96.9%**
101	of the worlds drawn on average and **42.9%** at its worst.
102	
103	**Two things to read off this.** First, the design's own tables get *markedly better* under the
104	additive rate on the question the spike exists for: worst `.2043 → .0420`, and the share over `.005`
105	`6.63% → 5.36%`. An additive rate is less sensitive to *when* a cause arrived, because mis-timing
106	one cause adds an error rather than multiplying into the others. Second, it is still not enough:
107	5.36% fails the 99% bar, so **the sampler is still required**, exactly as round one concluded.
108	
109	The sampler now clears the bar at **50 000** worlds rather than 200 000, which is four times
110	cheaper, and that is what the timing below uses.
111	
112	### The milliseconds half — `timing_add.py`
113	
114	The same twenty-claim map as round one (`ve_cost.layered_dag(20, 3, seed=1000)`), the same
115	observation, 24 slices, one world *with its range*. Round one's figures on the same map are in the
116	last column.
117	
118	**Every arrow helps** (no arrow holds a claim back):
119	
120	| | forward pass | exact solve | sample | **(b) total** | **(a) total** | round one, (b) |
121	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
122	| 1 version | 5.4 ms | 4.4 ms | 55 ms † | **10 ms** ✓ | **65 ms** ✓ | 213 ms ✓ |
123	| 200 versions | 26.9 ms | 12.4 ms | 58 ms | **39 ms** ✓ | **97 ms** ✓ | ≈38 s ‡ |
124	| 2 000 versions | 224.4 ms | 80.4 ms | 55 ms | **305 ms** (1.0×) | **360 ms** (1.2×) | — |
125	
126	**Three claims hold a claim back** — the density the biggest real generation run shows
127	(`inhibitors.py`):
128	
129	| | forward pass | exact solve | sample | **(b) total** | **(a) total** |
130	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
131	| 200 versions | 48.5 ms | 12.1 ms | 52 ms | **61 ms** ✓ | **113 ms** ✓ |
132	| 2 000 versions | 404.5 ms | 81.6 ms | 52 ms | **486 ms** (1.6×) | **538 ms** (1.8×) |
133	
134	*Sample column: 50 000 worlds over the twelve claims the evidence can reach, with the exponentials
135	taken once up front. ✓ = inside 300 ms. (a) = the exact core plus one sample, the correction shared
136	across versions.*
137	*† the sample was measured at 200 and at 2 000 versions, where it came to 58 and 55 ms; it does not
138	depend on the version count, so 55 ms is carried into the one-version row rather than measured
139	there. ‡ round one measured 9 584 ms at **fifty** versions at 24 slices; 38 s is that multiplied
140	out, not a measurement.*
141	
142	**The two costs that dominate, and how they behave.**
143	
144	- The **forward pass** is now linear in the versions and tiny per version: 0.13 ms per version with
145	  no arrow holding back, 0.20 ms with three. Round one's was 14.4 ms per version *at 12 slices* and
146	  191 ms at 24.
147	- The **sample** is a fixed cost however many versions the range has, because the correction is
148	  shared (§5). 55 ms at 50 000 worlds, 215 ms at 200 000.
149	- An **arrow that holds a claim back** still forces an enumeration over the days it might have
150	  arrived on, and that is the one place the cost still multiplies: on the same map, three such
151	  arrows cost 1.8× the forward pass, eight cost 5.4×, and the generator's own ten (up to three on
152	  one claim) cost **70×** — 15.9 s at 2 000 versions. Real maps carry at most one per claim.
153	
154	### The verdict
155	
156	| | holds .005 on 99%? | inside 300 ms with 200 versions? | with 2 000 versions? |
157	|---|---|---|---|
158	| (b) the design's tables | **no** (5.36% over) | yes, 39–61 ms | no, 305–486 ms |
159	| **(a) the sample, 50 000 worlds** | **yes** (0.00% over) | **yes, 97–113 ms** | no, **360–538 ms** |
160	
161	**Kill, still — and by a distance a named relaxation now covers.** Round one found that a range
162	needs 2 000 versions to hold a band's ends to two significant figures; at 2 000 versions the
163	winning candidate is 360 ms with every arrow helping and 538 ms at a real inhibitor density. Round
164	one's nearest miss was 3.0 s. This one is **360 ms**.
165	
166	**What relaxing the criterion to a named value would buy:**
167	
168	| relaxation | what it buys |
169	|---|---|
170	| budget **600 ms** for one world with its range | (a) passes at 2 000 versions at every inhibitor density measured |
171	| budget **400 ms** | (a) passes at 2 000 versions when no arrow holds a claim back; still 1.3× over at a real density |
172	| **200 versions** instead of 2 000 | (a) passes today at 97–113 ms. Round one measured the cost: a band's ends then wander a tenth of the band's own width — one significant figure, not two |
173	| a band printed to **one** significant figure | the same thing, said honestly on the screen instead of in the engine |
174	
175	**The nearest unmeasured headroom**, named so nobody has to guess: the exact solve takes 80 ms at
176	2 000 versions because it runs one elimination per claim — twenty passes. The standard way to get
177	every claim's number is two passes over a junction tree. If that saves what it usually saves, (a)
178	at 2 000 versions with every arrow helping lands near 295 ms. **I did not build it and I did not
179	measure it.**
180	
181	---
182	
183	## 3. What the hypothesis gets wrong
184	
185	Point by point, because the coordinator asked for it plainly.
186	
187	**1. "Calibration is closed form for every shape, no bisection."** *Half right.* It is closed form
188	for every arrow that **helps** a claim along, at every shape:
189	`added rate = [ln(1 − q0) − ln(1 − q1)] / (the arrow's shape added up over the window)`.
190	It is **not** automatically closed form for an arrow that holds a claim back, because such an arrow
191	cannot add a negative rate. The coordinator's own sketch — scale the rate by a factor raised to the
192	shape — needs a root find for an impulse or a ramp. I used a different scaling that **is** closed
193	form: the rate is multiplied by `1 − (1 − share) × shape`, which is the same thing at full strength
194	and interpolates linearly as the shape rises. It saturates: `30.0%` of the holding-back arrows in
195	the adversarial set could not hold back enough to reach their stated chance and were clamped at
196	"suppress the rate entirely while on" (`candidates_add.py`). The multiplicative form saturates too,
197	for the same reason — a cause cannot suppress a rate on days it is not on — but it saturates later,
198	which is where the two models are furthest apart (§4).
199	
200	**2. "Cost proportional to causes × slices, not slices-to-the-power-of-causes."** *Right for the
201	causes that help, wrong in general.* Every arrow that holds a claim back multiplies the forward
202	pass by about the number of slices, because the rate is additive over helpers only *given* the
203	inhibitors' days. Measured: `.13 ms` per version per range with none, `.20 ms` with three on the
204	map, `.60 ms` with eight, `7.9 ms` with the generator's ten. **This is the one place the design can
205	still be made slow**, and it is why `inhibitors.py` matters.
206	
207	**3. "The shape integrals do not depend on the version."** *Right, twice over.* Read off the
208	product: `_draw` takes `priors` and `strengths` and nothing else, `_version_priors` draws from
209	`claim.prior` and `_version_strengths` from `arrow.strength`
210	(`backend/src/katalyst/domain/propagation.py`; the provenance spread in the evals worktree,
211	`feat-04b-evals/.../propagation.py:1509`, draws strengths only). No lag, shape or half-life is ever
212	redrawn. And measured: many versions in one pass equals one version at a time to **0.0**.
213	
214	**4. "The winning sampler gets cheaper too."** *Wrong as first measured, right after one change.*
215	Reading the same arrays gave **355 ms** for 200 000 worlds against round one's **222 ms**, because
216	the survival chance had to be exponentiated once per world. Taking the exponentials once per
217	version up front — the rate adds over causes, so the survival chance is a *product*, and a product
218	of pre-exponentiated arrays needs no exponential at all — brings it to **215 ms**, and to **55 ms**
219	at the 50 000 worlds the accuracy actually needs. So the objection in round one §3 does go away,
220	but not for the reason given: it goes away because the sampler no longer needs the
221	slices-to-the-power-of-causes table in memory, not because reading it is cheaper.
222	
223	**5. "It is *literally* Kent's decision R6."** *R6 is necessary, not sufficient.* R6 fixes what the
224	model is **asked** — the claim's chance with no cause on the map, and each arrow's chance with that
225	one cause at the start of the window. Both rates consume exactly those two numbers and reproduce
226	them exactly. R6 does not say how **two** causes combine, and that is the whole difference between
227	the two models. It is a separate decision and it is Kent's.
228	
229	---
230	
231	## 4. What the change of model moves — `model_diff.py`
232	
233	**The worked example, for a finance reader.** A claim stands at 10% on its own. Two separate causes,
234	each of which *alone* would take it to 40% by the same deadline. Both happen on day one.
235	
236	| | neither cause | one cause | **both causes** |
237	|---|---|---|---|
238	| **additive — independent routes** | .100 | .392 | **.590** |
239	| **multiplicative — round one** | .100 | .392 | **.910** |
240	
241	*The additive number in words.* With no cause the claim fails 9 times in 10. One cause cuts that to
242	6 in 10 — so that cause removes a third of the ways it could fail. Two independent causes each
243	remove a third, so `.90 × (.60/.90) × (.60/.90) = .400` of the failure is left, and the claim
244	happens **.600** of the time. (The table reads `.590` rather than `.600` because the cause is placed
245	at the middle of the first slice rather than at day zero; both models show the same `.392` for one
246	cause, so the comparison is clean.)
247	
248	*The multiplicative number in words.* Each cause multiplies the rate by about five; both together
249	multiply it by twenty-five. The claim reaches 91%.
250	
251	**Which is right?** Neither, in general — it is a statement about the world. The additive form says
252	two causes are two separate ways for the same thing to happen, and knowing one has fired does not
253	make the other more potent. The multiplicative form says they reinforce. **What is not arguable is
254	that nobody stated the reinforcement**: the model is asked two numbers per arrow and neither of them
255	is about what happens when two causes coincide, so the amplification is put there by the engine's
256	choice of form and not by anything anyone said.
257	
258	**What is lost.** Genuine reinforcement cannot be expressed. *"Hormuz reopens"* and *"OPEC+
259	restraint holds"* may really be worth more together than apart for Brent, and under the additive
260	rate they are not. The honest remedy if a map needs it is a named interaction term on the pair,
261	which is a third number to elicit — and nobody has priced whether a model can state it coherently.
262	
263	**What is gained**, besides the cost: a claim's number can never be pushed past what its causes
264	severally justify, and the arithmetic is the familiar independent-routes rule a finance reader can
265	check by hand — as above.
266	
267	**How far apart, across the set** (140 maps, both judged exactly, 24 slices, middle day; claims by
268	number of causes: 155 with none, 244 with one, 109 with two, 52 with three):
269	
270	| every map — both choices at once | mean | median | 99th pct | worst | share > .05 |
271	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
272	| no edit (560) | .0060 | .0002 | .0688 | .1073 | 2.7% |
273	| *Suppose* (4 480) | .0051 | .0000 | .0902 | .3397 | 2.9% |
274	| *This happened* (4 480) | .0082 | .0003 | .1043 | .2437 | 4.4% |
275	
276	Worst: trial 38, *Suppose* `c1`, read on `c2` — additive `.4559`, multiplicative `.1162`. That is an
277	**inhibitor** case, not a helper case: the multiplicative form suppresses far harder while a cause
278	is only partly on. Isolating the helper choice, on the 20 maps of 140 where every arrow helps:
279	
280	| only maps where every arrow helps | mean | median | 99th pct | worst | share > .05 |
281	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
282	| no edit (80) | .0061 | .0004 | .0490 | .0634 | 1.2% |
283	| *Suppose* (640) | .0046 | .0000 | .0740 | .1809 | 2.0% |
284	| *This happened* (640) | .0088 | .0004 | .0870 | .1494 | 4.8% |
285	
286	**So: two separate decisions, and the second is the louder one.** How helping causes combine moves
287	the median number by `.0004` and about 1 in 20 numbers by more than `.05`. How an arrow that holds a
288	claim back works moves the worst case to `.34`. A claim with one cause is identical under both, and
289	half the claims on these maps have one cause or none.
290	
291	---
292	
293	## 5. Does *This happened* still need the sampler, and can the correction be shared?
294	
295	**Still needed.** The design's tables under the additive rate leave 5.36% of *This happened* numbers
296	off by more than `.005`, worst `.0420` (§2). Better than the `.2043` they left under the
297	multiplicative rate, and still not 99%.
298	
299	**And the correction is now shareable, which it was not.** This closes round one's own open item.
300	Round one measured the correction's version-to-version movement only on easy maps and said plainly
301	that a map where the correction is large had never been checked. Trial 33 is that map
302	(`hardmap.py`, 200 versions each):
303	
304	| trial 33, *This happened* on `c1`, read on `c3` | correction | how much it moves across versions | the answer's own spread |
305	|---|---|---|---|
306	| multiplicative rate, inputs drawn wide | .1172 | **.0805** | .1644 |
307	| multiplicative rate, inputs drawn narrow | .1732 | **.0544** | .0864 |
308	| **additive rate, inputs drawn wide** | **.0020** | **.0020** | .0748 |
309	| **additive rate, inputs drawn narrow** | **.0014** | **.0008** | .0323 |
310	
311	Under the multiplicative rate, one correction shared across a whole range would have been wrong by
312	up to `.08` on a band end — **round one's assumption fails on exactly the map round one flagged.**
313	Under the additive rate it is `.002`, and sharing is honest. On three other hard maps the two rates
314	are closer (trial 65: `.0286` moving `.0121` against `.0210` moving `.0095`; trial 15 about equal;
315	trial 17: `.0194` moving `.0092` against `.0140` moving `.0062`), so the collapse on trial 33 is the
316	extreme, not the rule — but it is the case that decides whether the shortcut is allowed at all.
317	
318	This is load-bearing for §2: the sample is a fixed 55 ms **because** it is taken once for a whole
319	range. If it had to be redone per version, 2 000 versions would cost 110 seconds.
320	
321	---
322	
323	## 6. What the decision record would have to say — sentences ready to paste
324	
325	These are offered only if Kent takes the additive rate; nothing here is settled.
326	
327	> **How two causes combine.** Each cause is an independent route by which the claim may come about:
328	> the causes add to the rate at which it happens, so the chance none of them brings it about is the
329	> product of the chances that none of them severally does. Two causes that each alone take a claim
330	> from 10% to 40% give 59% together, not 91%. Causes do not amplify one another; if a map needs
331	> that, it needs a third elicited number, and version one does not have one.
332	
333	> **How an arrow that holds a claim back works.** It scales the rate down while it is on, in
334	> proportion to its shape, calibrated from its own stated chance. An arrow cannot hold a claim back
335	> on days it is not on, so a very strong one saturates; measured on the adversarial set, 30.0% of
336	> such arrows could not reach their stated chance and were clamped.
337	
338	> **What it costs to compute.** A claim's table is an average taken one cause at a time, so a
339	> twenty-claim map with 2 000 versions takes 224 ms for the forward pass where the previous form
340	> took tens of seconds. An arrow that holds a claim back is the exception: it multiplies that claim's
341	> share of the cost by about the number of slices. Every real map checked carries at most one per
342	> claim.
343	
344	> **Where the versions ride.** A version redraws only the stated chances, never a lag or a shape, so
345	> the shape integrals are computed once for a whole range and a version enters as a scalar.
346	
347	---
348	
349	## 7. What I did not check
350	
351	- **The additive rate above four claims, for accuracy.** The judge is not computable there; the
352	  twenty-claim numbers are cost only.
353	- **The junction-tree solve** named in §2 as the nearest headroom. Not built, not measured.
354	- **A named interaction term** for two causes that genuinely reinforce (§4). Not built, and nobody
355	  has priced whether a model can state one coherently.
356	- **The exponential form of an arrow that holds a claim back** (`factor` raised to the shape), which
357	  is what the coordinator sketched. I measured the linear form instead, because it is closed form;
358	  the exponential one would need a root find and would saturate later, which is where §4's worst
359	  case comes from.
360	- **Whether real generated maps stay at one holding-back arrow per claim** once the prompt is
361	  changed to ask *what would stop this step* — which stack 05's freeze intends to do. Today's counts
362	  are from a prompt that never asks.
363	- **The `when` table under the additive rate.** Round one measured the arrival-day error under the
364	  multiplicative rate; the sampler's construction is unchanged, so it should carry over, but I did
365	  not re-run it.
366	- **The versions-per-range study under the additive rate.** Round one's 2 000 is used here as given.
367	  The band's width depends on the model, so the number could move.
368	- **I ran no test suite, no server, no browser and no paid call.** Nothing in the repository outside
369	  `plans/` was changed.
370	
371	---
372	
373	## Owed once stack 04 has landed
374	
375	Nothing. This round wrote no product code and no chapter.

# Spike 05-0, round two — the additive rate

**2026-09-21 · one read-only Opus agent · no file in the repository or any worktree was changed
outside `plans/`.** Every number below is printed by a script in
`plans/analysis/scripts/spike-05/observe/round2/`, named beside it; raw output in `logs/` there.
No paid call, no server, no browser, no test suite. Round one is
`2026-09-21-spike-05-observe.md`, and its scripts are the parent directory, imported here and not
edited.

**The hypothesis being tested, in one paragraph.** Round one killed the engine design on cost: at
twenty claims and two hundred versions, the forward pass that builds the yes/no tables took 2.9
seconds against a 300 ms budget, and most of that was enumerating every combination of a claim's
causes' arrival days. The coordinator's hypothesis is that the enumeration is forced by the
*shape of the rate* — round one's model made a claim's rate **multiplicative** in its causes,
which does not separate by cause — and that if causes instead **add** to the rate, each an
independent route by which the claim may come about, the chance the claim has not happened becomes
a product with one factor per cause, so an average can be taken one cause at a time.

---

## The verdict in six lines

1. **The hypothesis is right about the arithmetic, and the measurement is decisive.** The forward
   pass on the twenty-claim map at two hundred versions goes from **2 879 ms to 27 ms** — and that
   is at 24 slices, where round one's number was 9 578 ms for *fifty* versions (`timing_add.py`).
2. **Still a kill on the criterion as written — but the miss is now 1.2×, not 10×.** At the version
   count round one found a range needs (2 000), the winning candidate is **360 ms** against a
   300 ms budget. At 200 versions it is **97 ms and passes both halves**.
3. **The accuracy winner is unchanged and is now cheaper to be sure of.** The weighted forward
   sample with the exact solve as a control variate holds `.005` on **100.00%** of *This happened*
   numbers at 50 000 worlds (round one needed 200 000). The design's tables alone still fail, at
   **5.36%** off by more than `.005` (`candidates_add.py`).
4. **A side-benefit nobody predicted:** the additive rate also *shrinks the error the spike was
   sent to measure*. The design's worst *This happened* gap falls from `.2043` to **`.0420`**.
5. **And it closes round one's own open item.** On the hard map, sharing one correction across a
   whole range was **not** honest under the multiplicative rate — the correction is `.12` and moves
   by `.08` from version to version. Under the additive rate it is `.0020` and moves by `.0020`
   (`hardmap.py`). Sharing is what makes the sampler affordable, so this matters.
6. **The cost is a modelling choice Kent must make, not a free win.** Causes no longer amplify each
   other: two causes that each alone take a claim from 10% to 40% give **59%** together under the
   additive rate and **91%** under the multiplicative one, from the same stated numbers
   (`model_diff.py`). §4 puts both sides.

---

## 1. Is the additive core sound? — `check.py`

Five things, run before any number below was believed.

| | worst gap |
|---|---|
| **one cause at a time == averaging the full table over combinations of causes** | **4.4e-16** |
| **the forward pass agrees with the same full-table average** | **2.1e-15** |
| **many versions in one pass == one version at a time** | **0.0** |

Those three are the hypothesis's actual claims, and they hold to machine precision.

Two more compare the slice machinery with a dense integral of the rate itself. What is left there
is the **slice grid**, which the additive and multiplicative models share, and it shrinks as the
slices multiply:

| slices × points inside each | calibration reproduces its stated chances to | the machinery is the rate to |
|---|---|---|
| 24 × 8 | 1.8e-2 | 1.9e-2 |
| 24 × 32 | 5.5e-3 | 4.6e-3 |
| 48 × 8 | 6.4e-3 | 8.3e-3 |
| 48 × 32 | 1.8e-3 | 2.7e-3 |

The hard case is a spiky impulse — a half-life of about a day against a slice 2.5 days wide. Round
one measured the same effect on the multiplicative model and it is the reason its §4 recommends the
middle-day convention, which is used throughout here.

---

## 2. The kill criterion again, literally

### The accuracy half — `candidates_add.py`

The same 140 adversarial four-claim maps as round one, the same stated chances, 24 slices, the
middle-day convention, 17 queries each — read under the additive rate, judged by the same
method (exact over the whole joint of arrival slices, given the additive tables).

| *This happened*, 4 480 numbers | mean | 99th pct | worst | share > .005 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **(b) the design's prior-timing tables** | .00103 | .0127 | **.0420** | **5.36%** |
| (a) sample 50 000, read straight off the worlds | .00120 | .0053 | .0103 | 1.43% |
| **(a) sample 50 000, with the control variate** | .00028 | .0020 | **.0042** | **0.00%** |
| (a) sample 200 000, with the control variate | .00014 | .0010 | .0017 | 0.00% |

| no edit (560) | mean | 99th pct | worst | > .005 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| (b) the design's tables | .00019 | .0039 | .0117 | 0.71% |
| (a) sample 50 000, corrected | .00033 | .0019 | .0025 | 0.00% |

| *Suppose this is true* (4 480) | mean | 99th pct | worst | > .005 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| (b) the design's tables | .00004 | .0010 | .0116 | 0.13% |
| (a) sample 50 000, corrected | .00017 | .0015 | .0027 | 0.00% |

Effective sample size — how many equally-weighted worlds the weighted sample is worth — is **96.9%**
of the worlds drawn on average and **42.9%** at its worst.

**Two things to read off this.** First, the design's own tables get *markedly better* under the
additive rate on the question the spike exists for: worst `.2043 → .0420`, and the share over `.005`
